memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not hate a fellow Israelite in your heart. Rebuke your neighbour frankly so you will not share in their guilt.'" - Lev 19:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This verse follows the one about slander, and the connection is deliberate. Having forbidden talking behind someone's back, God now says what to do instead: talk to their face.

Rebuke your neighbour frankly. Not silently resent them. Not complain to everyone else. Go and speak honestly to the person themselves.

Most of us find this almost impossible. We would rather carry irritation for years than have one uncomfortable conversation. So resentment settles in the heart — and God addresses that too: do not hate a fellow Israelite in your heart. Silence is not neutrality. Unspoken grievance curdles.

Jesus gave the same instruction with striking simplicity: if your brother or sister sins, go and point out their fault, just between the two of you (Matt 18:15). Just the two of you. Not a coalition. Not a group message.

Notice the reason God gives: so you will not share in their guilt. Saying nothing while someone damages themselves is not kindness. It makes us complicit.

But note the word frankly, not harshly. Speaking the truth in love (Eph 4:15). Both halves.

Who do you need to speak to rather than about?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there resentment you have carried instead of speaking honestly?
2. Who have you talked about rather than talked to?
3. What makes honest conversation feel so difficult for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me courage for honest conversations rather than silent resentment. Help me speak truth with real love, and free my heart from what I have been carrying. Amen.
